chain.label: FAA certification relied solely on a drawing review of the gust lock/interlock design
chain.trigger: compliance with 14 CFR 25.679(a)(2) was found by review of the drawings; there was no functional test of the design of the G-IV gust lock/throttle interlock system

chain.label: Gust lock/throttle interlock did not limit throttle movement to the intended 6 degree warning threshold
chain.trigger: postaccident testing found that, with the gust lock handle in the ON position, the forward throttle lever movement that could be achieved on the G-IV was 3 to 4 times greater than the intended TLA of 6 degrees

caused_by.evidence: the FAA missed opportunities to detect the inadequate design of the gust lock system during the G-IV's certification because the FAA relied solely on a review of engineering drawings

chain.label: Night flight reduced the conspicuity of the red gust lock handle
chain.trigger: the accident occurred at night in lower lighting conditions, when the color red is less conspicuous and would, therefore, be less easily noticed by either pilot

chain.label: Flight crew habitually skipped checklists, failing to disengage the gust lock and perform the flight control check
chain.trigger: the flight crew neglected to disengage the airplane's gust lock system... before initiating takeoff, the pilots neglected to perform a flight control check; the pilots had neglected to perform complete flight control checks before 98% of their previous 175 takeoffs

chain.label: Gust lock remained engaged, locking the elevator, ailerons, and rudder through taxi and takeoff roll
chain.trigger: the FDR recorded restricted motion of both the elevator and rudder throughout the taxi and attempted takeoff, consistent with the flight crew failing to disengage the gust lock system

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew failed to disengage the gust lock system as called for in the Starting Engines checklist and failed to conduct a flight control check as called for in the After Starting Engines checklist

chain.label: Crew did not notice the gust lock handle position or the throttle restriction as the takeoff roll began
chain.trigger: the flight crew did not notice that the gust lock handle was in the ON position during taxi, line up, or the initial portion of the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: the gust lock handle was in the ON position during taxi, line up, or the initial portion of the takeoff roll
the color red is less conspicuous [at night] and would, therefore, be less easily noticed by either pilot

chain.label: Throttle levers contacted the gust lock interlock, and EPR plateaued well below the normal takeoff setting
chain.trigger: the throttle levers were manually advanced to an initial PLA of only about 17.5 degrees, and the EPR achieved was about 1.42... this EPR plateau at a lower-than-normal level likely resulted from the throttles contacting the gust lock/throttle lever interlock

caused_by.evidence: the forward throttle lever movement that could be achieved on the G-IV was 3 to 4 times greater than the intended TLA of 6 degrees
the interlock restricted the throttle levers to about 50% of the range of movement that the flight crew typically used

chain.label: PIC did not reject the takeoff on encountering the throttle restriction, engaging the autothrottle instead
chain.trigger: the PIC did not immediately reject the takeoff; instead, he engaged the autothrottle, and the throttle levers moved slightly forward

caused_by.evidence: despite encountering this abnormal throttle lever restriction, the PIC did not immediately call out the problem or call for a rejected takeoff before engaging the autothrottle

chain.label: Gust lock handle's lock pin likely fractured under the autothrottle/manual load, letting EPR approach the target setting
chain.trigger: the lock pin in the gust lock handle was likely broken or compromised, allowing the throttle levers to move forward and the engines to attain an EPR value that approached the target setting

caused_by.evidence: as a result of the autothrottle engagement, and possibly due, in part, to manual forces applied to the throttle levers, the lock pin in the gust lock handle was likely broken or compromised

chain.label: Crew failed to notice the control yoke never moved from full forward toward neutral through 60-80 kt
chain.trigger: the PIC did not check the elevator for freedom of movement or notice that the control yoke was not moving from the full forward position to the neutral position as a result of the restriction imposed by the gust lock

caused_by.evidence: the elevator position recorded by the FDR remained constant at about 13 degrees trailing edge down as the airplane accelerated through 60 kts
the flight crewmembers had likely not previously experienced a problem with a locked elevator during takeoff, so they were probably not watching closely for elevator movement

chain.label: PIC repeatedly called out 'lock is on' but the SIC never replied, and neither pilot called for a rejected takeoff
chain.trigger: although the PIC repeatedly stated his concern about the status of the gust lock, the SIC never replied; neither pilot verbally commanded a rejected takeoff after this strategy proved unsuccessful

caused_by.evidence: when the PIC attempted to rotate the airplane, he discovered that he could not move the control yoke and began calling out '(steer) lock is on'
the only cue that something was wrong by that point was the displaced position of the yoke, a condition that the PIC apparently did not notice

chain.label: Flight crew delayed initiating the rejected takeoff until stopping on the runway was no longer possible
chain.trigger: the flight crew delayed applying brakes for about 10 seconds and further delayed reducing power by 4 seconds; therefore, the rejected takeoff was not initiated until the accident was unavoidable

caused_by.evidence: this lack of two-way communication was inconsistent with best practices for CRM... the flight crew delayed initiating a rejected takeoff until the accident was unavoidable; this delay likely resulted from surprise, the unsuccessful attempt to resolve the problem through the use of the FPSOV, and ineffective communication

chain.label: Airplane overran the end of runway 11
chain.trigger: it overran the end of runway 11 during a rejected takeoff... rolled through the paved overrun area and across a grassy area

caused_by.evidence: the rejected takeoff was not initiated until the accident was unavoidable

chain.label: Airplane struck nonfrangible approach lights, the localizer antenna, and the perimeter fence, coming to rest in a ravine
chain.trigger: collided with approach lights and a localizer antenna, passed through the airport's perimeter fence, and came to a stop in a ravine

caused_by.evidence: after leaving the paved runway overrun and entering the grass, the airplane collided with structures that were not mounted on frangible supports

chain.label: All seven occupants died of smoke inhalation and thermal injuries in the postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the postcrash fire, which erupted immediately, spread rapidly, and prevented the occupants from escaping; cause of death for both pilots, the flight attendant, and three of the four passengers was 'smoke inhalation and thermal injuries'

caused_by.evidence: the impact forces from the accident were survivable, but the cabin and cockpit environment quickly deteriorated due to the postcrash fire
